_comment: Which scorer each lane invokes, and how.  Edited by hand when an engine's
CLI changes; read by bin/fidelity/engines.py.  A lane with pinned:false
refuses to plan -- see the module docstring for why guessing flags is worse
Verify a lane after editing:  bin/measure-local --probe-engines

sealed-ep8.name: k6_student_capture + k6_kld_report (sealed EP8 lane)

timing.provenance: ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED. No per-window wall clock was recorded for the sealed EP8 lane in a form this runner can cite. The figure is a deliberately conservative placeholder so the cost estimate errs high rather than low; the max-runtime coherence check uses it, and the printed estimate labels it. Replace it with a measured number from a sealed-lane run receipt.

notes: This is the lane K6 and Q4 were measured with, and the only one whose
flags are verified against the file in this checkout.  EP size is
env-driven (QP_GLM53_EP_SIZE) and the launcher's --nproc-per-node must
match it.  Requires the patched quant_pipeline tree (--pipeline-root)
and a BF16 skeleton carrying config.json + model.safetensors.index.json,
because the capture binds inventory.config_sha256/index_sha256 to the
LOCAL files.
--surface packed dereferences packed_root from the checkpoint's own
materialization-receipt.json.  For a third-party artifact that path is
on the producer's machine; see hfmeta.sniff_surface, which detects this
before any money is spent.
sealed-ep8.surfaces_note: k6_student_capture.py --surface {packed,dione}, verified against the file. 'packed' additionally needs the payload store to be PUBLISHED in the repo; sniff_surface traps the case where the receipt's packed_root points at the producer's machine. There is no 'tr3-published' reader.

streaming.name: stream_score (single-GPU streaming lane)
streaming.unpinned_reason: VERIFIED 2026-08-28 against the real file (sha256 b74118042e7f221d536f98a0de5a28f094422bc96cdd49cb54b5ac905260acae, recovered from /home/jl_fs/glm53-k6/tools/). The engine EXISTS, and the contract below was wrong: it takes --teacher, not --panel, and --source {checkpoint,payload-store,dione}, not --surface. Two deeper blocks, neither of which a flag_map can fix: (1) --profile choices are k6|k8|k6k8 and the controller sends 'k4' for this lane, which argparse rejects outright; (2) every source path resolves to a PACKED ROOT and hard-requires contract.json + inventory.json + mtp-adapter-receipt.json + payload-store/{objects,choices} plus a --bf16 tree, i.e. this campaign's own encode output. A third-party HF repo (surface 'tr3-published', payloads inline in the shards) has none of those, and --source dione is disabled in this build. So the streaming lane cannot score a stranger's quant until a tr3-published reader exists. Pinning the flags would only move the failure to after the rental.
contract: --checkpoint PATH        the artifact to score
--panel PATH             the fetched teacher/panel directory
--out PATH               receipts + tokenwise-kld output root
--surface NAME           packed | dione | tr3-published
--reduce-order {fp32,native}   fp32 is the validated setting: the
window-0 KLD delta vs the sealed EP8 lane is
+1.5076e-5 at 99.80% argmax agreement
--cold-run N             labels the capture receipt
--roles final            which panel roles to score
it must emit a tokenwise-KLD tensor whose sha256 is the determinism
evidence (NOT a receipt-file hash -- see registry DET-001)
notes: Known properties from the validation run, which the receipt must
disclose: bitwise cross-topology parity is impossible (routed-expert
combine order moves logits rms 0.26-0.28); streaming runs ARE bitwise
identical to each other, so determinism holds WITHIN the lane; peak
34-47 GB on one H200 as currently scheduled.

timing.provenance: MEASURED on the K6 streaming panel run (stream-k6/runs/stream-run1, 1x H200 spot, --decode-cache none): capture-receipt elapsed_seconds 11,018.9 for 25 windows = 7.35 min/window; cold run 2 was 10,488.7 s = 6.99 min/window. Two cold runs of a 231 GB payload store therefore cost 5.97 GPU-hours (~$11.89 at $1.99/GPU-h), not the ~$7.50 the earlier estimate implied. The BF16-floor lane (--source native, 609 GB read per window) measured ~8.3 min/window on the same box class.

streaming.surfaces_note: stream_score.py --source {checkpoint,payload-store,dione,native}. The first three all resolve to a packed root with contract.json + inventory.json + mtp-adapter-receipt.json + payload-store/{objects,choices}, and --source dione raises 'not enabled in this build'. --source native (added 2026-08-29) is the exception: it needs NO packed root, only a --bf16 tree and a sealed release inventory (--inventory), because it scores the un-quantized BF16 experts themselves -- the measurement FLOOR of this lane, see k6/BF16-FLOOR.md. It is not a reader for a stranger's artifact; there is still no 'tr3-published' reader.

local-mps.name: stream_score on Apple Silicon (MPS)
local-mps.unpinned_reason: VERIFIED 2026-08-28 against the real file: same packed-root and --profile blocks as the streaming lane, and NONE of the memory knobs this contract names exist. The engine has --vram-budget-gb (not --vram-budget), --slab-experts (not --expert-chunk), --stream-mode window-major (not --window-batch), and no --kld-device at all. Plus two Apple-Silicon constraints that must be honoured by whatever lands: MPS cannot do float64 AT ALL (not slowly -- torch raises TypeError), so the KLD accumulation must run on CPU; and 34 of 45 layers are Kimi-Delta linear attention whose only known fast paths are Triton/CUDA or a fused MLX kernel, so the torch/MPS forward is UNVERIFIED.
contract: everything the streaming lane requires, plus:
--device {auto,mps,cuda,cpu}
--kld-device cpu         MANDATORY on MPS. estimator.accumulation_dtype
is a comparability key input, so silently
degrading fp64 to fp32 would move the row into
a different comparability group. Refuse, do
not degrade.
--expert-chunk N         numerics-invariant memory knob
--window-batch N         numerics-invariant memory knob
--vram-budget GB         honoured as a hard bound
notes: Measured on a 128 GB M4 Max: the EXL3/TR3 decode is pure PyTorch (no
custom kernel, no exllamav3 build) and is BITWISE IDENTICAL on MPS and
CPU at both 4 and 6 bits, over full-size 8,388,608-element matrices.
So the local lanes carry NO device offset from weight decode; any
local-vs-sealed offset comes from the forward pass alone.
Consequence for the recipe: `pip install torch safetensors numpy
huggingface_hub` is sufficient locally. None of stage_k6.sh's
bootstrap (deadsnakes, CUDA 13, flash-attn, exllamav3) is needed.

timing.provenance: DERIVED from measured per-matrix decode on a 128 GB M4 Max (16.7 ms/matrix at 6 bits, 14.0 ms at 4 bits, MPS, int32 unpack) under the panel-batched layer-outer schedule, where the 36,288-matrix routed pass happens ONCE for the whole panel rather than once per window. That makes per-window time an amortisation, not a measurement: ~15 min for the whole 25-window panel. The forward pass itself (KDA/DSA/mHC on MPS) is UNVERIFIED and is not in this figure.

local-mps.surfaces_note: same engine, same packed-root requirement as the streaming lane.

local-cuda-budget.name: stream_score under a VRAM budget (consumer CUDA)
local-cuda-budget.unpinned_reason: VERIFIED 2026-08-28 against the real file: same packed-root and --profile blocks as the streaming lane. The budget knob is --vram-budget-gb, not --vram-budget; --expert-chunk, --window-batch and --nonrouted-residency do not exist (the engine has --slab-experts and a single --stream-mode window-major).
contract: everything the streaming lane requires, plus:
--vram-budget GB         hard bound, honoured not approximated
--expert-chunk N         numerics-invariant
--window-batch N         numerics-invariant
--nonrouted-residency {pinned,mmap,gpu}
the scatter-add over experts MUST be sequential in ascending expert
order. An atomicAdd-based scatter would make the result depend on the
memory knobs, which destroys the invariance the recipe promises.
notes: Peak for the panel-batched layer-outer schedule on GLM-5.3-Flash at
4bpw: 23.5 GB whole-layer, 25.5 GB at the solver's default fill for a
30 GB budget. The floor for ANY schedule is 4.6 GB, set by the lm_head
weight plus one window of fp32 logits -- neither shrinks with the
memory knobs.

timing.provenance: PROJECTED. No Blackwell hardware was available. Scales the measured Apple-Silicon decode by memory bandwidth (1.79 TB/s vs ~410-546 GB/s) and treats the run as I/O-bound on reading 176-254 GB once. Treat as an order-of-magnitude figure until someone runs it.

local-cuda-budget.surfaces_note: same engine, same packed-root requirement as the streaming lane.

bf16-floor.name: stream_score --source native (the lane's BF16 measurement floor)

timing.provenance: MEASURED on 1x H200 spot (IN2, 28 vCPU, 300 GiB cgroup) reading the 599 GB BF16 tree off a CephFS filesystem at ~1.05 GB/s with 28 reader threads: window 1 (cold, all 42 layers filled) 678 s; steady-state windows 483-549 s with --decode-cache ram holding 17 of 42 layers. See k6/BF16-FLOOR.md.

notes: This lane does not score a quant. It scores the UN-QUANTIZED BF16 experts through the
identical capture, so its panel mean is the FLOOR every quant measured on this lane
sits on top of. Subtract it (k6/tools/bf16_floor_summary.py) to state a quant's
quantization-attributable error.
It is the only stream_score source that needs NO packed root: --inventory (a sealed
quant-pipeline.glm-release-inventory.v1) plus the --bf16 tree is the whole input.
It is IO-bound, not decode-bound: 14.50 GB of routed BF16 per layer, 42 layers per
window. Size the box by filesystem read bandwidth and by 47.1 GB of VRAM, not by
matmul throughput.
Requires SM90-class or newer ONLY in the sense that the venv is pinned to torch
2.11.0+cu130; an instance whose driver predates CUDA 13 cannot run it at all
(observed on an A100-80GB image shipping driver 12080).
The workspace symlink farm (/workspace/artifacts/...) must exist before the run: the
sealed panel receipt declares those paths and the artifact identity check refuses
symlinked FILES while requiring the directories to resolve.
bf16-floor.surfaces_note: The official BF16 release tree itself (config.json + model.safetensors.index.json + shards). Not a reader for a third-party quant.
